thread.title: Microsoft’s bearish ‘death cross’ to finally appear, ahead of earnings - MarketWatch

title: Microsoft’s bearish ‘death cross’ to finally appear, ahead of earnings - MarketWatch
text:
Microsoft Corp., which climbed to the top of the heap of U.S. companies two months ago, will finally join its technology-heavyweight peers by producing a bearish “death cross” chart pattern.
Coincidentally, the death cross is set to appear on the day the software giant is scheduled to report fiscal second-quarter results.
Microsoft’s stock MSFT, -2.04% fell 2.3% in afternoon trade Tuesday, adding to Monday’s 2% drop. The two-day selloff comes as investors grew cautious about the technology sector, after chip maker Nvidia Corp. NVDA, -4.64% warned of a big revenue shortfall , with Chief Executive Jensen Huang calling the fourth quarter an “extraordinary, unusually turbulent and disappointing quarter.”
See related : Nvidia suffers slew of downgrades as analysts weigh sales warning .
Microsoft’s 50-day moving average, which many chart watchers use as a guide to the shorter-term trend, fell to $104.7608 on Tuesday from Monday’s $104.8474, according to FactSet. Meanwhile, the 200-day moving average, viewed by many as a dividing line between longer-term uptrends and downtrends, rose to $104.6726 from $104.6274.
Since the beginning of January, the 50-day moving average has declined by an average of $0.0690 per day, while the 200-day moving average has increased by $0.0630 a day, suggesting the 50-day moving average will cross below the 200-day moving average on a closing basis on Wednesday.
FactSet, MarketWatch Many on Wall Street believe a “death cross” marks the spot that a shorter-term pullback transitions into a longer-term downtrend.
The last time Microsoft’s 50-day moving average was below its 200-day moving average was Aug. 8, 2016, while the last “death cross” appeared on June 23, 2016.
After the last “death cross,” the stock fell 4.7% over the next two sessions, but was up 14% three months later. The one before that, the stock lost 1.7% before bottoming 6 weeks later, but was up 25.5% after three months.
Regarding Microsoft’s earnings report, which is due out after Wednesday’s close, the company has beat earnings expectations the past 10 quarters, according to FactSet, and beat revenue projections the past six quarters.
The stock has gained on the first trading day after earnings were reported in 15 of the past 20 quarters, by an average of 3.9%. The average of the five declines during that period was 4.3%.
Microsoft, which wrested the title of largest U.S. company by market-capitalization from Apple Inc AAPL, -1.04% in November, is the last of the large-cap tech stocks to avoid the bearish “death cross” fate.
Also read : Apple’s ‘death cross’ is first in 3 years, and last for FAANG stocks .
Here are the dates that a “death cross” appeared in the stock charts of the other tech heavyweights, and of the major market indexes.
• Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, -2.69% currently the second most valuable U.S. company: Dec. 12, 2018.
• Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, -0.91% the third most valuable U.S. company: Nov. 15, 2018.
• Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.04% the fourth most valuable U.S. company: Dec. 20, 2018.
• Facebook Inc. FB, -2.22% : Sept. 20, 2018.
• Intel Corp. INTC, -0.36% : Sept. 10, 2018.
• Cisco Systems Inc. CSCO, +0.46% : Jan. 25, 2019.
• Netflix Inc. NFLX, -2.01% : Nov. 19, 2018.
• Nasdaq-100 Index NDX, -0.96% : Dec. 3, 2018.
• S&P 500 index SPX, -0.15% : Dec. 7, 2018.
• Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.21% : Dec. 19, 2018.
Tomi Kilgore Tomi Kilgore is MarketWatch's deputy investing and corporate news editor and is based in New York. You can follow him on Twitter @TomiKilgore.
